name: Rishat Maksudov
tagline: Systems engineer with 4+ years of production C and C++ across networking, router firmware, and distributed block storage.
about: Systems engineer with 4+ years of production C and C++ across networking, router firmware, and distributed block storage. At Wellstor I write C++ services on top of SPDK (disk subsystem + metrics). At Huawei I worked on router firmware in C (NAT, ALGs, eBPF/NFQ-based wireless simulation) and in C++ (packet-filter optimization, large GoogleTest coverage). Active C++23 practitioner with a portfolio of personal projects.
meta_description: Portfolio of Rishat Maksudov - C/C++ Developer working on networking, low-level Linux internals, and distributed block storage.

experience.description: Write C++ services for a distributed block storage product built on top of SPDK (C).
achievements: Built the disk subsystem service in C++ - wraps SPDK with management commands and RPCs for volume splits, RAID creation / management, and related operations
Built the metrics service in C++ - Prometheus integration providing runtime observability over the disk subsystem
Designed a cross-node disk heartbeat in C++ to detect connectivity issues, plus an on-disk metadata layer so previously-added disks can be recovered on restart
Added per-module versioning so binary compatibility issues surface at runtime; maintained CMake, RPM .spec, systemd units
Wrote GoogleTest coverage in modern C++ across the disk subsystem; fixed an NVMe-path lock-up and several memory leaks using AddressSanitizer

experience.description: Worked on router firmware in C and C++; scope spanned a packet-filtering subsystem in C++, the NAT subsystem, and the eNSP Pro Lite simulator.
achievements: Worked on the packet-filtering subsystem in C++: optimized the rule-lookup hot path (longest-prefix matching for CIDR-masked rules like /24, /16) and reduced the memory footprint of the rule table
Wrote large amounts of GoogleTest coverage in modern C++ across NAT, ALG, ARP, and control-plane components

Led the local NAT effort with a small team of two, coordinating with a remote colleague at Huawei China; added the full CLI control surface for NAT, refactored and extended ALG handling for FTP, PPTP, RTSP and other protocols, and added new ALGs

Extended eNSP Pro Lite (enterprise network simulation platform) to cover our AP, SOHO router, IoT devices, and mobile stations; implemented virtual wireless connectivity using NFQ and eBPF; simulated signal strength, packet loss, and station roaming
Built ubridge (a variation of ebridge) to join interfaces across virtual devices into a single bridge, enabling interop with external network simulators
Partnered with DevOps to build a pytest + scapy system-test framework

experience.description: Worked on firmware in C and C++ for AP, IoT, and SOHO router devices, focused on the CLI / control plane.
achievements: Implemented IP address configuration and dynamic enable/disable of IP routes on address changes; added handling for link and physical/logical addresses
Built an ARP table with binary-tree fast lookup over an auto-expanding storage layer
Wrote GoogleTest unit tests in modern C++ covering the ARP table and surrounding control-plane code
